title: RACER: Risk-Aware Calibrated Efficient Routing for Large Language Models
claim: A two-phase pipeline first calibrates a risk threshold offline, then uses it online to select, run and aggregate model sets or abstain.
layout: 2 panels split by dashed line, left-to-right flow, threshold arrow bridging phases
description: The figure is split by a vertical dashed line into two phases. The left panel, titled Risk Calibration, flows top to bottom. A database icon for calibration data feeds a green box, Augmented Scoring and Set Construction (Offline), which has set-augmentation and score-augmentation sub-icons. Below it is a blue Risk Calibration box with a gauge icon for threshold tuning, and a warning icon marks the target risk level α entering from the left. A thick black arrow carries the threshold λ̂ across to the right panel, Model Routing. There, a test query goes to a Base Router, then to a green online scoring box with LLM icons and a red null-model bulb. A gray diamond asks whether only the null model was selected. Yes leads to an orange Abstain box. No leads to a gray Model Execution box, then to an orange Response Aggregation box (majority voting or weighted aggregation, with a temperature input), and finally to the Final prediction ŷ.
caption: Overview of the RACER paradigm. RACER operates in two phases. Risk Calibration (Left): The calibration module uses a labeled dataset Dcal and a user-specified risk level α. It augments the standard model space M with a null model m∅to construct augmented ground truth set G′. The threshold ˆλ is then computed to guarantee risk control. Model Routing (Right): During inference, the paradigm applies the calibrated ˆλ to the augmented scores of a test query x. This generates a prediction set Cˆλ(x). If the set contains only the null model, the system triggers abstention; otherwise, it proceeds to Response Aggregation, where the outputs of the selected standard LLMs are combined via majority voting or weighted aggregation to produce the final prediction ˆy.
abstract: Efficiently routing queries to the optimal large language model (LLM) is crucial for optimizing the cost-performance trade-off in multi-model systems. However, most existing routers rely on single-model selection, making them susceptible to misrouting. In this work, we formulate LLM routing as the $Î±$-VOR problem to minimize expected set size while controlling the misrouting risk, and propose a novel method -- RACER, extending base routers to output model sets that can be subsequently aggregated for improved output. In particular, RACER constructs nested model sets via augmented scoring and utilizes finite-sample concentration bounds to calibrate a threshold that allows for both variable set sizes and abstention. We theoretically prove that RACER achieves rigorous distribution-free risk control on unseen test data in a post-hoc and model-agnostic manner. Extensive experiments verify our theoretical guarantees and demonstrate that RACER consistently enhances downstream accuracy across a wide range of benchmarks.
